channel.title: The Missing Seat
channel.description: Evidence-based editorials asking who is missing, why it matters, and what can be done.

item.title: The Robe Doesn’t Erase What the Judge Knows
item.description: A judge’s recorded prejudice raises a question retirement alone cannot answer: What happened in the cases she already decided?

item.title: “Black-on-Black Crime”: Naming the Violence Without Hiding Its History
item.description: Violence within Black communities is real. So is the history that shaped where violence, poverty and disadvantage became concentrated.

item.title: What Can We Do to Make Justice Happen?
item.description: If injustice was built through laws, institutions and public choices, what can be done now?

item.title: The Class Construction After Reconstruction
item.description: Emancipation ended slavery. It did not erase the economic and social hierarchy built around it.

item.title: Nigger: The Word, the Law and the Line We Draw
item.description: The public often punishes America’s most infamous racial slur more readily than the hierarchy the word declares.

item.title: Power Is Not Proof of Superiority
item.description: Centuries of oppression prove that domination can be organized and preserved. They do not prove a racial hierarchy.

item.title: The Violence Behind the Reconstruction Amendments
item.description: The doctrine cannot be separated from the murders, rape, torture, massacres and political terror that constitutional protection was meant to confront.
